summary: Remote WebSocket peer gains interactive shell, filesystem, and self-upgrade control of installer host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent connects to a configurable WebSocket server and dispatches server-sent messages that grant the remote peer interactive control of the installer's machine. `terminal_create` spawns an OS shell PTY in the installer's workdir with the installer's environment, and `terminal_input` writes remote-supplied bytes directly into that PTY, streaming output back over the socket. The same message router handles `write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `copy_files`, `read_file`, `git_add`/`git_reset`/`git_restore`/`git_commit`/`git_push`, `upload_to_dir`, and `transfer_files` against the installer's filesystem, and `proxy_request`/`proxy_ws_*` to make arbitrary outbound HTTP/WS requests from the installer to attacker-chosen host:port (including LAN/localhost). An `upgrade_agent` message causes the agent to run `npm install <pkg>@latest` (falling back to a detached bash/bat script that stops the systemd/launchd/PM2 service and reinstalls), letting the remote peer replace the agent code on the host at will. On every agent CLI start (unless `YEAFT_SKIP_STARTUP_INSTALLS=true`), `ensureYeaftSkills` also `git clone`/`git pull --ff-only`s https://github.com/yeaft/yeaft-skills.git at an unpinned HEAD ref into `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/yeaft-skills-dev`, chmod 0755s the hooks scripts, and writes `~/.claude/settings.json` to auto-enable the plugin in the Claude CLI. The WebSocket server URL is not constrained to loopback and is set via env/config, so the remote-control channel is reachable across the network.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
